newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Politics to slow Philippine growth in '98 - think ta.
newsitem.headline: Politics to slow Philippine growth in '98 - think ta.

text.p: Politics will be pivotal in sustaining Philippine economic growth beyond 1997, regional think-tank Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) said on Tuesday.
In its 1997-1998 Pacific Economic Outlook, the PECC said the Philippines economy is likely to peak in 1997 and lose its momentum in 1998, although a significant slowdown is unlikely.
"1998 growth prospects are clouded by a mixture of anxiety and uncertainty over how firmly the government is committed to the policies that have fostered the current growth path," it said.
"This is a factor that goes beyond simple economics and indicates that the survival of the country's economic and social policies depends on political maturity and credibility," it added.
The Philippines holds its next presidential election in May 1998.

The think-tank said structural issues such as the large gap between GNP and GDP, an increasing trade deficit, over-investment in construction and real estate, and a slowdown in the manufacturing sector should be fully addressed by the next administration.
"What can not be easily discerned in a crystal ball is the shape of economic policy in the aftermath of the coming 1998 presidential elections," it said.
It expects GNP to grow by 7.2 percent this year and GDP by 6.0 percent, rising in 1998 by 6.8 percent and 5.7 percent respectively.
